# ChunkLand

> Land-claim plugin for Folia 26.2. Players fence off a claim with a selection wand; every attempt to break, place, open, use, fight inside, or enter that claim is then decided individually rather than by a one-time check when the chunk loads.

Current release: **0.1.0**, published at <https://github.com/smile-minecraft/ChunkLand/releases/tag/v0.1.0>. Supports **Folia 26.2** on **Java 25** with **AceLib 1.3.0** required. Paper is not a supported runtime. All permission nodes default to `op`.

## Start here

- [README (English)](https://github.com/smile-minecraft/ChunkLand/blob/main/README.md): what the plugin decides, how to build and install it, and the two defaults to change before opening a server.
- [Documentation index (English)](https://github.com/smile-minecraft/ChunkLand/blob/main/docs/en/README.md): pick the guide by what you are doing.

## Notes for agents integrating with ChunkLand

- The API is published on JitPack under the **root** coordinate `com.github.smile-minecraft:ChunkLand` (not a module one): add `maven { url = uri("https://jitpack.io") }` to your repositories and depend on `com.github.smile-minecraft:ChunkLand:v0.1.0` with `compileOnly`, then declare `depend: [ChunkLand]` in your own `plugin.yml`. That artifact is the API jar alone — no Bukkit, SQL or AceLib, and no plugin class. Bundling it is wrong — the server already loads those classes.
- **The entry-point class is in the plugin jar, not the API jar.** `getReadApi()` and `publicEventBus()` are declared on `com.smile.chunkland.ChunkLandPlugin`, which is not in the JitPack artifact, so any code that imports, casts or declares that type fails to compile with the JitPack dependency alone. Add a second `compileOnly` entry — `compileOnly(files("libs/chunkland-plugin-0.1.0.jar"))`, with `chunkland-plugin-0.1.0.jar` downloaded from <https://github.com/smile-minecraft/ChunkLand/releases/download/v0.1.0/chunkland-plugin-0.1.0.jar> — or point `compileOnly(files(...))` at a locally built `chunkland-plugin/build/libs/chunkland-plugin-0.1.0.jar` instead of JitPack. That plugin jar embeds the API module, so it covers both needs in one entry. Both entries stay `compileOnly`; `Bukkit` comes from the paper-api compile dependency a Paper plugin already declares, and neither jar ships Bukkit.
- ChunkLand does **not** register itself in Bukkit's `ServicesManager`. `getRegistration(ChunkLandApi.class)` returns `null`. Get the API from the plugin instance instead: `((ChunkLandPlugin) Bukkit.getPluginManager().getPlugin("ChunkLand")).getReadApi()`.
- `getReadApi()` never returns `null`. It returns a holder that reads as an empty registry before the first enable and after disable, and it keeps observing later changes, so it is safe to cache for the lifetime of one enable.
- `publicEventBus()` is `null` **only** before the first enable. A disable does not clear it: the accessor keeps handing back the previous enable's bus, and that stale bus silently receives no further events. Register listeners on a handle you acquired in the current enable, and re-acquire after every enable — do not carry a handle across a disable, because it goes quiet instead of throwing.
- Eight of the nine `ChunkLandApi` methods work: `getLandSnapshot`, `getSubLandSnapshot`, `getOwner`, `getProtectionDepth`, `can`, `isReady`, `getLandAt`, `decideAtBlock`. One does not: `getRule(LandId, LandRuleType)` always returns empty, because `getReadApi()` injects a rule lookup that returns `Optional.empty()`. Do not build features on it.
- For a protection check at a block, call `api.isReady()` first, then `api.decideAtBlock(actor, worldId, x, y, z, action)` and compare `.outcome()` with `PermissionState.ALLOW`. It returns the same decision ChunkLand's own listeners enforce (admin bypass, owner guarantee, covering subland, member and group bindings, defaults, land rules). Wilderness answers `ALLOW`; an index not yet confirmed, a disabled plugin or any lookup failure answers `DENY` instead of throwing. A `null` actor, world id or action throws `NullPointerException`.
- `getLandAt(worldId, chunkX, chunkZ)` returns the land owning a chunk from the in-memory index. Empty means wilderness only while `isReady()` is `true`.
- `can(UUID, LandId, ProtectionActionType)` gives a land-level decision through the same permission context as the protection engine, without sublands (no block position). It returns `false` while `isReady()` is `false` or the land is unknown.
- Every read takes exactly one volatile snapshot, does no I/O, never loads a chunk, and returns immutable values. It is safe to call from any thread. There is no way to observe a half-applied mutation through it.
- Event dispatch is synchronous on the publishing thread. A throwing Pre listener cancels the mutation and it produces zero side effects; a throwing Post listener is logged and isolated while the committed mutation stands.
- Event listeners must return immediately: no blocking, no I/O, no waiting, and no Bukkit world access outside the matching Folia thread. Post listeners run on the async continuation after the commit.
- There is no supported write entry point. The type `com.smile.chunkland.api.mutation.ChunkLandMutations` exists and declares `submit(MutationRequest)`, and the plugin contains an implementation of it, but `ChunkLandPlugin` exposes no accessor for it — only `getReadApi()` and `publicEventBus()`. Do not plan on a programmatic claim.
- Player references in commands accept a raw UUID, then an exact case-sensitive online name, then an offline-player lookup that runs on an async executor and only answers for players the server already knows. Names that never joined do not resolve.
- Protection is fail-closed: until the registry is hydrated, an empty result means unknown, not wilderness, and the answer is deny.
- Land rules — PVP, explosions, fire, mob griefing, fluid flow, pistons, hopper transfer, mob spawning — cannot be changed from any interface. Inside a land, fluid flow, pistons, hopper transfer and both kinds of mob spawning follow vanilla; PVP, explosions, fire spread and burn, and mob griefing are denied. A piston, fluid or hopper that reaches across a land boundary — in either direction — is always refused. The `rule-defaults` block in `config.yml` is a commented example and is not wired.
- Entry defaults to `ALLOW`. Strangers can walk into a loaded claim until the operator sets `subject-defaults.global.ENTRY: DENY`. Entry bans override the default in the other direction.
- There is no reload command. Configuration changes need a server restart.
